newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi calls for swift review of pensions.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi calls for swift review of pensions.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi on Wednesday called for a review of the 1995 pension reform as soon as possible to settle doubts about the effectiveness of the overhaul.
The reform, signed by then prime minister Lamberto Dini, unions and employers, is officially meant to come under review in 1998, but Ciampi indicated he would like to see this process quickened.
"The sooner (the review) is done, the better to resolve the doubts and uncertainties which damage the full recovery of trust in our economy," Ciampi wrote in a letter to Rome newspaper Il Messaggero.

Unions have said they don't want the review to be brought forward, but employers' organisation Confindustria said earlier this month that without a swift overhaul of the reform, the government would not achieve its ambitious 1997 financial goals.
Employers argue that the reform introduces changes to Italy's heavily indebted state pensions' system too gradually and say the planned timetable for changes must be speeded up.
Ciampi said that a review of pension plans alone would not be enough to guarantee the stability of state accounts.

"One shouldn't forget another aspect, which I think is even more important -- the reform of public administration," Ciampi wrote. "Civil society will no longer tolerate the waste of money, time and human resources caused by the scarcely efficient state," he added. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
